audit.whatIsWrong: The interaction the whole lane turns on was never stated. Riot's Shifting Sands text: Azir shields himself and dashes TO ONE OF HIS SAND SOLDIERS, and if he hits an enemy champion he instantly readies a new soldier and HALTS HIS DASH. The page never says the dash requires an existing soldier, and never says a champion in the path stops it short.
audit.why: No soldier on the ground means Azir has no dash and no escape at all. That is the single fact that tells an Aurora player when to commit, and it turns 'is Shifting Sands down?' into something visible on screen rather than a count in your head.
audit.corrected: Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1 and 1100 range, but it can only travel to a soldier that already exists — clear the soldier and he cannot cast it. Standing in the path halts the dash where you are.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit E and W text, ranges, cooldowns)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text and mid both claim 'Between Worlds phases you clean through Emperor's Divide's shockwave'. Aurora's R has no phase and no untargetability — Riot gives it a leap, a shockwave, a slow zone and a teleport across that zone. Emperor's Divide is also not a 'shockwave': it is a wall of soldiers that charges forward, knocking back.
audit.why: A player who believes their ultimate cancels his will hold a 140s cooldown for a 120s one and get displaced anyway.
audit.corrected: Emperor's Divide is 120s at rank 1 and casts at only 250 range, so he has to be next to you. It knocks you away rather than holding you, so it buys him distance — the punish is walking back in.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief ownerKit R text, enemyKit R text, range and cooldown)

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read Skill on all seven rows while the content layer and the packet agreed on Aurora for levels 1 through 6 and Azir from first item. Two answers to the same question.
audit.why: Conquering Sands is 14 seconds at rank 1 costing 70 mana, his soldiers deploy at 525, and Shifting Sands is 22s and conditional on a soldier existing. That is a weak early kit against a 900-range Q. His Q reaching 6s at rank 5 alongside items is what flips the later rows.
audit.corrected: Aurora at 1 through 6 (4/10, then 5/10 at level 6), Azir at first item (6/10) and two items (7/10) — the full layer moved onto the content and packet chart, side, rating and why together per row.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet reports zero sequencing cues in the entire matchup, and breakdown.cooldowns held no digit.
audit.why: Defect catalogue item 3. The numbers here are unusually decisive — a 14-second Q at rank 1 is one of the longest basic-ability cooldowns in the lane.
audit.corrected: Conquering Sands 14s at rank 1 falling to 6s at rank 5, Shifting Sands 22s at rank 1, Emperor's Divide 120s at rank 1 and 90s at rank 3, Arise! a flat 1.5s.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Twin Drift' is not an Aurora ability (spikes[0].text, early). spikes[2].text also recommends Shieldbow, an attack-damage lifesteal item, on an ability-power mid, and credits Aurora with an 'early DoT spike' she does not have.
audit.why: Fabricated ability name and an item that does not belong in the build the same field's own report[8] describes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions Shurima's Legacy — Azir can summon the Disc of the Sun from the ruins of allied OR enemy turrets.
audit.why: It changes how a fight around a fallen tower is priced, on either side of the map, and it is his only unique map mechanic.
audit.corrected: Noted in the late-game text: a fallen turret is a turret he can bring back.

notes:
The most valuable finding here is one Riot states plainly and the page never did: Shifting Sands dashes to one of his Sand Soldiers, so with no soldier on the ground he cannot cast it, and if the dash hits an enemy champion it halts there. That converts the page's advice from 'count his 22 seconds' into something visible on screen. It also fixes the packet's 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' defect at the root.

Level chart: the full layer read Skill on all seven rows while content and packet.levelChart agreed on Aurora through level 6 and Azir from first item. Two agreeing sources against one flat template, so the full layer moved onto them — side, rating and why proposed together per row. content win[] was already correct and untouched.

SuspectNames: all three flags are false positives — 'Emperor's Divide' and 'Between Worlds' are real names. Two of the three lines were still wrong for other reasons, since both claimed Between Worlds phases through his ultimate.

Unverified and left alone: whether Emperor's Divide's soldier wall blocks Aurora's Q missile, and whether it can block or cancel her W leap or her R teleport. The wall carries a 'terrain — blocks paths and dashes' flag and both of Aurora's mobility spells carry 'walls can deny', which is suggestive, but Riot's own text for the ultimate says only that the soldiers charge forward knocking back and damaging. Given the brief's own calibration example is a missed Azir wall interaction, this one is worth someone confirming rather than guessing — it would be the single highest-value line left in the matchup.
